title: Units, a unit LM, and a speech adapter for a frozen LLM
brief: Turn frames into deduplicated k-means units and score them with a bigram unit LM, then stack Whisper frames, project them into a frozen language model, and train the projector with a loss masked to the transcript.
hints: assign_units: expand the squared distance as |x|^2 - 2 x.c + |c|^2 so one matrix product gives every frame-to-centroid distance, then take np.argmin along the centroid axis.
kmeans: record the inertia right after each assignment, before you move the centroids, and leave a centroid alone when no frame chose it.
deduplicate: a run starts wherever a unit differs from the one before it; np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, u[1:] != u[:-1]]) finds those starts, and np.diff of the starts gives the durations.
unit_bigram_lm: np.add.at(counts, (seq[:-1], seq[1:]), 1) counts every neighbor pair, including repeated pairs, which plain fancy-index assignment would count once.
stack_frames: slice off the last T % k frames, then one reshape to (B, T // k, k * d) puts k neighbors side by side, because the frames are contiguous in memory.
next_token_loss: compare logits[:, :-1] with labels[:, 1:], and pass ignore_index=-100 to F.cross_entropy so masked positions add nothing to the sum or the count.
